scenes.headline: Measure Without Climbing!
scenes.concept_takeaway: Line of sight and horizontal level form a right triangle to find heights.
scenes.quick_tip: Always draw the horizontal base line first before marking any angle!
scenes.narration: Wait a second... how do you measure the height of Qutub Minar without climbing it with a giant measuring tape?! Sounds impossible, right? Actually, all you need is a shadow and one tiny angle! Welcome to Heights and Distances—where simple right triangles turn you into a master surveyor!

scenes.headline: Elevation Vs Depression
scenes.concept_takeaway: Looking up creates Angle of Elevation; looking down creates Depression.
scenes.formula_badge: Angle of Elevation = Angle of Depression (Alternate)
scenes.quick_tip: Both angles are ALWAYS measured with the horizontal line, never vertical!
scenes.narration: Imagine spotting a sixer flying over the cricket stadium! When you tilt your chin up from the flat ground... that's the Angle of Elevation! Now picture looking down from your balcony at a parked bicycle. You look down from the horizontal sky line... and boom! That's the Angle of Depression!

scenes.headline: The Golden Ratios
scenes.concept_takeaway: Use 30°, 45°, and 60° side ratios to solve board problems in seconds.
scenes.quick_tip: At 45°, Height always equals Base distance! Instant 1-second answer!
scenes.narration: Want to solve five-mark board numericals in ten seconds flat?! Forget long calculations! Just memorize three magic triangles! At forty-five degrees, height and shadow are exact twins—one to one! At sixty degrees, height becomes root-three times the base! Spot the angle, plug the ratio, and boom—full marks!

scenes.headline: Topper Exam Trap!
scenes.concept_takeaway: Subtract observer height first and never mark depression with the wall.
scenes.formula_badge: Total Tower Height = h (Triangle Height) + Observer Height
scenes.quick_tip: Trap Alert: Never mark Angle of Depression between line of sight & tower!
scenes.narration: Hold on! Don't fall into the number-one CBSE exam trap! Ninety percent of students mark the Angle of Depression against the vertical building wall. Wrong! Always draw a dotted sky-horizontal line first! And if a tall observer is given... never forget to add their height at the end!
